criteria.criterion: MCP and review-bot tests prove startup bindings stay stable across ambient mutation while each new operation receives the intended fresh non-secret snapshot.
MCP inbound bearer/OAuth material remains request-local and absent from startup/operation snapshots, serialization, logs, caches, child environments, and tool schemas.
Review-bot decision-bearing auth is validated before job/provider work, only the selected integration is constructed, and revoked/missing/conflicting auth never falls back to another principal.
Static binding replacement is observed only after process restart/redeploy; native refreshable capability behavior remains SDK-owned.
Partial/rejected Langfuse/OTLP auth disables telemetry without changing the underlying operation result, while security/load-bearing auth remains fail-closed.

findings.detail: The attestation in the ticket explicitly states 'No AWS creds in this autonomous session' and uses instrument=static-analysis rather than a live AWS deploy/E2E canary run. The required provenance elements (change/run ids, startup binding kinds, vote/result, retry counts, timestamp, redacted diagnostics from a live AWS canary) are not recorded. The attestation defers the live AWS deploy/E2E canary to RP-04 S7 AC6, meaning this criterion is not satisfied in this ticket's snapshot.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment with the live AWS review-bot deploy/E2E canary run: include the Gerrit change URL/id, CI run id, startup binding kinds observed, vote/result, retry counts, timestamp, and redacted diagnostics from the actual AWS canary execution (infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh). The attestation must name these specifics from a real AWS-credentialed run, not a static-analysis substitute.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
